Short answer: you need *some* way to fill `api/.dev.vars`, and 1Password is just the fastest one for you. Looking at the template, here's what actually matters:

**The only secrets you can't make up** are the GitHub App credentials (`GITHUB_CLIENT_ID`, `GITHUB_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GITHUB_APP_NAME`, `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) — that's what powers "Sign in with GitHub" and the repo sync that pulls your checkpoints in. Without those, you can't get data into the app at all.

**Everything else is dummy-able or optional** for what you're trying to see:
- `ENCRYPTION_KEY` / `SESSION_SECRET` / `ENTIRE_WEB_API_TOKEN` — any random strings work locally
- `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY_ANALYSIS` — only powers the AI analysis pipeline; transcript rendering doesn't need it

- `frontend/.env` — the PostHog values can be blank/dummy; only `VITE_API_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8787` matters

So your two options:

1. **`! op signin` then `! mise run secrets`** — since you're on the entire.io team, the shared dev GitHub App lives in the Shared vault and this takes 30 seconds. This is the intended path.
2. **No 1Password**: copy `api/.dev.vars.template` → `api/.dev.vars`, fill the dummy-able values by hand, and create your **own GitHub App** (callback `http://localhost:8787/...`, generate a private key) for the five GitHub fields. **Trails are display-layer for agent data, not agent-specific.** A trail is a PR-like workflow object that groups checkpoints/sessions by branch. Everywhere it touches agents, it flows through the shared registry we already updated:

- `checkpoint-mapper.ts` extracts agents dynamically from session JSON (`sessions.map(s => s.agent)`) — your `"Goose"` string passes straight through

- Recap, activity aggregator, and contribution charts all build their `Record<AgentId, number>` maps from `AGENT_IDS` — goose is in that list now, and typecheck passing proves no exhaustive map was missed
- DB columns store agent as a plain `string` — no enums, no SQL agent lists

2. **Sandbox runs / runner launchers** — these *launch* agents in cloud sandboxes (fix-CI, evaluations), opt-in per repo via `.entire/runners/v2/` configs, and currently Claude-centric. Goose sessions recorded via your CLI never touch this path — it's only relevant if someday you wanted entire.io to *spawn* goose in a sandbox, which would be a separate (much bigger) project.

## What

Adds [Goose](https://github.com/block/goose) (Block's open-source coding agent) as a recognized agent, so sessions checkpointed via the new `entire-agent-goose` external agent binary render properly instead of falling back to Unknown.

- **`GooseParser`** (`api/src/lib/transcript-parsers/goose-parser.ts`): parses Goose's stored transcript format — the `goose session export --format json` document the external agent binary materializes. Renders user prompts, merges consecutive assistant messages into turns, folds `toolResponse` blocks into their originating `toolRequest` tool calls, classifies tools (shell/fileOps/search/agent), extracts skills from `load_skill`, and extracts the model from `model_config`.
- **Attribution**: `goose` added to `AGENT_IDS`/labels (api) and the frontend agent registry, with a goose SVG avatar and lime color classes (light + dark). Checkpoint metadata already arrives with `"agent": "Goose"`, which now normalizes to the goose identity.
- Registry test coverage for `goose`/`Goose`/`GOOSE` normalization and a full parser test suite using a fixture captured from a real goose 1.37.0 session.

## Why

The Entire CLI side ships `entire-agent-goose` (entireio/external-agents) — checkpoints from it sync here but previously attributed to "Unknown" and the transcript hit the fallback parser.

## Testing

- All transcript-parser unit tests pass (258, incl. new goose + registry cases)
- `tsc --noEmit` clean in `api/` and `frontend/`
- Parser verified against a real committed checkpoint from a goose session: `"Goose"` → `goose` attribution, 2 rendered messages, 9 tool calls with results, model extracted, no fallback/warnings
- Previously-synced goose checkpoints re-parse automatically via the existing `hasNonFallbackParser` re-parse path

## Notes

- `website/` agent registry intentionally untouched (it doesn't list Kiro either — appears curated)
- The goose avatar SVG is hand-drawn placeholder art; happy to swap for official brand assets if we have usable ones

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

input.command:
gh pr create --title "Add entire-agent-goose: Goose external agent" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## What

Adds `entire-agent-goose`, an external agent binary integrating [Goose](https://github.com/block/goose) (Block's open-source coding agent) with Entire — built via the repo's `/entire-external-agent` skill (research → write-tests → implement).

**Capabilities**: `hooks`, `transcript_analyzer`, `transcript_preparer`, `token_calculator`, `compact_transcript`

- **Hooks** — `install-hooks` writes a project-scope goose plugin (`.agents/plugins/entire/hooks/hooks.json`) forwarding goose's native `SessionStart` / `UserPromptSubmit` / `Stop` / `SessionEnd` lifecycle events to `entire hooks goose <verb>`. Goose discovers project plugins from its working directory; no global goose config is touched.
- **Transcripts** — goose stores sessions in SQLite with no per-session file; `prepare-transcript` (and best-effort on stop/session-end) materializes one via `goose session export --format json` next to goose's sessions.db. Transcript positions are message indexes since every export rewrites the document.
- **Tokens** — from the export's accumulated session totals (per-message counts are NULL in goose's DB; no cache split — documented in AGENT.md).
- **Compact transcripts** — converts the export to Entire Transcript Format so conversations render in `entire explain --full` and the web UI.

All research is verified against real goose 1.37.0 hook captures and exports (see `AGENT.md` + `scripts/verify-goose.sh`, which probes via a throwaway workspace without touching global config).

## Design note worth maintainer eyes 👀

The session dir is goose's data dir (`~/.local/share/goose/sessions`), deliberately **outside the repo**: Entire attributes a session to the first registered agent whose `get-session-dir` contains the transcript path, and a repo-local dir like `.entire/tmp/goose` nests inside amp's/kiro's `.entire/tmp` — with `entire-agent-amp` installed, Amp silently claimed every goose session and TurnEnd checkpoints were skipped. Since **amp and kiro share `.entire/tmp` today**, the same misattribution risk exists between them; the CLI may want longest-prefix matching in `AgentForTranscriptPath`.

## Shared harness fixes (benefit all agents)

- `e2e/entire/entire.go`: `RewindList` tolerates the deprecation banner newer entire versions print before the JSON
- `e2e/lifecycle_test.go`: `SessionPersistence` resolves the session dir via the agent's `get-session-dir` instead of hardcoding `.entire/tmp`, and only counts files fresher than the test start

## Testing

- Protocol compliance (`external-agents-tests verify`): **29/29 pass**
- Lifecycle e2e (`E2E_AGENT=goose`, real goose + real provider): **all 8 scenarios pass** (enable, hooks install, single/multi prompt checkpoints, session persistence, rewind pre/post-commit, interactive tmux session)
- Unit tests: hook parsing, install/uninstall round-trip, transcript analysis, token calc, compact conversion — all against payloads captured from real goose sessions

## Companion PRs

- entirehq/entire.io#2354 — web rendering + attribution for goose
- entireio/cli (branch ready) — `--full`/`--verbose` external-agent transcript display fix
